findings.result: The outlined jellyfish rim is the open dome silhouette's base edge and attachment line for the tentacles. It is not an enclosed counter, ring opening, or independently identifying interior mark.

The prompt does not mandate copying every outlined stroke as a filled knockout. It says an enclosed object can retain identifying marks as cutouts, structural openings stay open, and explicitly says filled is a shadow rather than an inversion and may drop unreadable hatch.

The bug-filled anchor retains an interior vertical body mark, but that mark is inside an enclosed bug body. This differs morphologically from a jellyfish silhouette boundary where tentacles attach. The anchor alone does not establish a compulsory horizontal jellyfish cutout.

Both paints preserve the bell silhouette and three tentacles. The absent filled rim is a deliberate construction delta whose acceptability needs matched same-morphology evidence; it is not automatically a lost semantic feature.

decision: No production prompt correction is justified. The written controls already distinguish structural openings and identifying marks from optional detail and warn against mechanically inverting every stroke.

recommendedExperiment.purpose: Test whether a filled jellyfish rim knockout improves native recognition and house fit without presuming it is required.
recommendedExperiment.design: Render the same terminal-bound filled program unchanged and a single no-redraw geometry counterfactual that adds only a bounded horizontal rim knockout while preserving bell and tentacle topology. Present both anonymously with the same matched native anchors to independent critics; ask first for free description, then native legibility, family fit, and defect evidence.
recommendedExperiment.controls: Keep outlined fixed, use exact 16px and 2x light/dark proofs, bind program/proof hashes, randomize order, retain disagreements and the existing rejected A151 denominator.
recommendedExperiment.limitations: This would be one exposed development example and cannot establish a universal twin rule, critic qualification, or output acceptance.
